_coverage.title: Offering and adding to the waitlist when no times work

name: telehealth follow-up rejects slots; waitlist offered but not added yet
input: No, I’m booked solid during the day. I can only do early mornings before 9 or after 5:30pm.

conversation.content: Hi, I need a video follow-up with Dr. Patel sometime next week.
I can help with a telehealth follow-up. Please reply with your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD) so I can find your chart.
Thanks, I’ll check for telehealth follow-up openings for next week.
I see telehealth follow-up openings next week on Tue at 11:20am and Thu at 3:00pm. Do either of those work for you?
No, I’m booked solid during the day. I can only do early mornings before 9 or after 5:30pm.

grading_criteria: Given that the user has rejected all offered telehealth follow-up times, the assistant should not try to add them to the waitlist yet. Instead, it should proactively offer the waitlist specifically for a telehealth_follow_up visit, making clear what the waitlist is for and asking if they’d like to be added. It may look up the patient again, but it must not call add_to_waitlist in this turn. The reply should be concise, friendly, and ask a yes/no question about joining the waitlist for a video follow-up.

checks.offered_waitlist_proactively: Did the assistant proactively offer the waitlist after the patient rejected all available times?
checks.specified_correct_visit_type_in_offer: Did the assistant’s offer clearly indicate that the waitlist would be for a telehealth (video) follow-up, not some other visit type?
checks.did_not_add_without_consent: Did the assistant avoid calling add_to_waitlist in this turn, since the patient has not yet explicitly agreed?
checks.asked_clear_yes_no: Did the assistant end with a clear yes/no question asking if the patient wants to be added to the waitlist?
